children: Health officials are investigating a salmonella outbreak linked to broccoli sprouts produced by Idaho-based Evergreen Fresh Sprouts, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said.
There have been 22 cases including two hospitalizations.
The CDC said the sprouts were distributed at food co-ops, restaurants, foodservice customers and grocery stores in Idaho, Montana and Washington.
The agency said the outbreak doesn't appear to be related to salmonella and E. coli outbreaks traced to alfalfa sprouts from Minnesota-based Everything Fresh Sprouts.
The Food and Drug Administration and state traceback investigations identified Idaho's Evergreen Fresh Sprouts as the common grower of the broccoli sprouts, the FDA said.
The recalled sprouts were packaged in plastic bags or plastic clam-shell containers, the agency said.
